project_description:
Provision of Engineering Professional Support Services at Koeberg Nuclear Power Station for the
Nuclear Engineering Contract for Scope A (Defined Scope) & Scope B (Ad-hoc Services)
reason_for_expansion:
Nuclear Engineering and the Nuclear Operation Unit at large has experienced a skills diminution due to
retirements and resignations in the recent years. This has resulted in a backlog being created and an
increased strain on the remaining personnel to cover the increased workload. Various projects are
being implemented at KNPS to support the LTO safety case as demonstrated to the National Nuclear
Regulator (NNR), such as the Steam Generator Replacement (SGR) project, Scoping and Ageing
Management Evaluation of Long-Term Operation Assessment (SALTO) and Periodic Safety Reviews
(PSR) and so forth. The Nuclear Engineering department does not have sufficient resources to provide
all the services required to manage all the engineering deliverables for these projects within the
timelines required in addition to the departmental daily operations. Therefore, additional engineering
services are needed to provide technical support to the engineering functions within nuclear
engineering. The need for the NE Professional Service suite of contracts has grown due to more urgent
tasks being identified and additional end users now utilising the panel that were not initially considered
at the time of conceptualisation of the panel services.

reason_for_expansion:
Majuba is a coal-fired PowerStation comprising of 6 operational units. The Power Station is also

efficient and effective manner to meet the demands of Majuba Power Station. The Contractor is to
continue ensuring that the Coal Plant is Available & Reliable to such that zero load losses are taken on
the units due to the Coal Plant. Furthermore, the Contractor must continue ensuring that the Tippler
Plant experiences no delays due to maintenance on either the Tippler or downstream plant.

reason_for_expansion:

upcoming outages. Boiler tubes are long lead items that typically require six to eight months for
delivery. With the current lead times, it is imperative that we act swiftly to ensure that we have the
necessary materials on hand to prevent any delays in the maintenance schedule. The process of
initiating a new contract is already underway, but the time required to establish a new contract may
result in us missing critical deadlines for the upcoming outages. Therefore, it is in our best interest to
proactively modify the current contract to meet our immediate needs while concurrently working on the
new contract. Kriel is facing an upcoming outage which is Unit 6 that demands immediate attention and
without additional boiler tubes, the risk that could have significant operational and financial implications
to the Station.

plant cleaning contract which was placed in August 2024. On 12 November 2024, the supplier
indicated their desire to terminate the contract citing their inability to cope with the sharp rise in
minimum wage and would incur losses post December payroll. Kendal Power Station sought
assistance from other Stations to assist but unfortunately Arnot is the only Station in such a position
with a coal plant cleaning contract. Kendal Power Station has now begun the process to place a new
long-term contract but due to the duration of placing a long-term contract as well as it being the rainy
season, the Station will be at risk should it not have cleaning resources in place. The termination of
